moduleTitle: Leveraging the Command Line Interface (CLI) in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain how to use the Testim CLI to streamline automation workflows.
Install the Testim CLI and run tests from it.
Use a configuration file to control which tests a CLI run executes and with what overrides.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Installing and running via the CLI

elements.description: Use a supported Node.js LTS/runtime and install the npm CLI package. The documented global workflow is npm install -g @testim/testim-cli followed by testim connect; a local package install needs the applicable local launcher rather than assuming a global testim command appears.

elements.term: Why use the CLI at all
elements.description: CLI supports configured test selection, grids, parallelism, data sets and CI invocation. It is not the sole mechanism for all non-local execution: the editor can run a single grid test and Scheduler can trigger configured matrices.

A config file (e.g. testimConfig.js) is created and passed to the CLI runner as a parameter, pointing to its path if needed. It can define the project ID, token, labels selecting which tests to run, the Selenium grid to use, and base URL overrides.

bulletPoints: Documented global install: npm install -g @testim/testim-cli; connect and configure the runner.
The CLI unlocks cross-browser, parallel, CI/CD, branch-scoped, and full data-driven runs.
A config file (e.g. testimConfig.js) drives which tests run and how — project ID, token, labels, grid, base URL overrides.

elements.title: Test selection & execution control
items: --label / -l, --name / -n, --testId / -t, --suite, --suite-id, --test-plan — different ways to select which tests a run should execute.
--rerun-failed-by-run-id — re-executes only the tests that FAILED in a specific previous remote run, instead of the whole suite.

For a single intersection filter, intersect requested selection with the label/suite. Multiple intersection flags use documented OR semantics by default; --intersect-with-operand controls AND/OR for label intersection flags.
--timeout is the individual test limit in milliseconds (10-minute default, three-hour maximum), not a guaranteed total suite duration.
--retries — sets how many times a failed test automatically re-runs.
--set-retention — configures how many days (1–10) results are retained before deletion.

bulletPoints: --rerun-failed-by-run-id re-runs only what failed last time, not the full suite.
Individual test timeout: 10-minute default, three-hour maximum; total execution is distinct.
Single versus multiple intersection filters have different composition; check the default OR and label operand setting.

examPitfalls.title: Expecting a plain editor run to do everything the CLI can
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Trying to achieve cross-browser or parallel execution from the editor Play button alone.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose CLI or Scheduler for configured matrices. A single editor grid run is supported, while ordinary embedded-data editor playback uses the first data set. Inspect the actual runner and results.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which command performs the documented global npm installation of Testim CLI?

options.text: By downloading a standalone .exe installer only.
It comes pre-installed with every Testim project automatically.

practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented global workflow installs the npm CLI package and uses testim connect afterward. A supported Node.js runtime and execution configuration are required.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented global npm installation command.
optionExplanations.B: The documented npm workflow is not exe-only.
optionExplanations.C: A project does not automatically install the machine’s CLI runtime.
optionExplanations.D: This is not a Python package workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What can a Testim configuration file (e.g. testimConfig.js) control when passed to the CLI runner?

options.text: Project ID, token, labels selecting which tests run, the Selenium grid, and base URL overrides.
Nothing — configuration files are not supported by the CLI.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about which tests run, where, and against what.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A config file can include the project ID, token, labels to specify which tests to run, the Selenium grid, and base URL overrides — controlling what the CLI run actually executes and against what environment.

optionExplanations.A: Execution config controls more than display theme.
optionExplanations.B: These are supported run configuration fields.
optionExplanations.C: Run configuration is not personal-account password management.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Testim CLI flag lets you re-run only the tests that failed in a specific previous remote run, without re-running the tests that already passed?
practiceQuiz.hint: It targets a specific prior run's failures, by that run's ID.
practiceQuiz.rationale: --rerun-failed-by-run-id re-executes only the tests that failed in a given previous run, letting you re-verify fixes without re-running the entire suite.

optionExplanations.A: This flag targets failures from the specified prior run.
optionExplanations.B: General retry count is different from selecting a prior run’s failed tests.
optionExplanations.C: This disables timeout retry rather than selecting prior failures.
optionExplanations.D: Branch selection does not itself select only prior failures.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What is the documented default and maximum individual test timeout for the Testim CLI --timeout flag?
practiceQuiz.hint: It's measured in milliseconds under the hood.
practiceQuiz.rationale: --timeout sets the individual test limit in milliseconds, with a 10-minute default and three-hour maximum. This is distinct from total suite duration or temporary execution-list status.

optionExplanations.A: These are the documented individual test bounds.
optionExplanations.B: These bounds are not the documented defaults/maximum.
optionExplanations.C: The CLI has a documented default limit.
optionExplanations.D: These bounds do not match the documented test timeout.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With one selected suite and one intersection label (no other intersection flags), which combination narrows execution to tests in that suite that also carry the label?

options.text: --suite-id alone, since it already implies labels.
This isn't possible with the Testim CLI.

practiceQuiz.hint: There's a flag specifically named for intersecting selection criteria.
practiceQuiz.rationale: --suite with a single --intersect-with-label narrows the requested suite to label matches. Multiple intersection flags have separately documented default OR composition; do not generalize this single-filter example to every combination.

optionExplanations.A: Suite selection alone does not impose the specified label filter.
optionExplanations.B: One suite plus one intersection-label filter implements the stated selection.
optionExplanations.C: A plan does not automatically apply this requested intersection.
optionExplanations.D: The documented intersection filter supports this selection.

quickRecap.value: Global npm CLI install plus testim connect; use supported Node.js and actual runner configuration.
Unlocks cross-browser, parallel, CI/CD, branch, and full data-driven runs.
Project ID, token, labels, grid, base URL overrides — passed as a CLI parameter.
--rerun-failed-by-run-id targets one prior run's failed tests.
Individual test limit: 10 minutes by default, up to three hours via --timeout in milliseconds.
